summary: Build a Scope 3 inventory, supplier engagement plan, and disclosure data workflow. Explore this practical five-day training programme.
lede: Scope 3 emissions management helps procurement, supply chain, and sustainability professionals build value-chain inventories and connect emissions data to sourcing. The course develops practical skills in category mapping, emissions calculations, supplier data requests and evidence checks, carbon-informed procurement, and reduction planning, with exercises to create an inventory, supplier engagement plan, and review checklist.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for value-chain emissions data, supplier relationships, procurement decisions, or sustainability reporting. It suits people who need to connect GHG Protocol accounting with practical supply chain workflows. This course is designed for: Procurement managers embedding emissions criteria into sourcing and supplier selection. Supply chain directors overseeing value-chain data collection and reduction priorities. Sustainability officers coordinating Scope 3 inventories and emissions-reduction plans. ESG reporting leads mapping supplier evidence to CSRD and IFRS S2 disclosures. Category managers assessing supplier emissions alongside cost, quality, and resilience. Supplier sustainability managers developing engagement plans and emissions-data requests. GHG accountants screening Scope 3 categories and documenting calculation assumptions. Responsible sourcing specialists reviewing supplier performance and corrective actions. Carbon data analysts validating activity data and maintaining inventory workpapers. Public-sector procurement leads integrating value-chain emissions into tender evaluation.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with procurement, supply chain operations, sustainability reporting, or greenhouse gas accounting is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with spreadsheet software if you want to complete the Excel-based exercises using your own tools. Use only data you are authorized to share.
